situation:
You are the co-founder and general manager of GOLDEN HOUR DUMPLINGS, a two-year-old food truck that sells hand-folded dumplings at office lunch stops and weekend markets. The investor (judge) put in the company's first and only round of funding, which is nearly spent, and meets with you each month to review where the business stands.

Two weeks ago the company signed a three-year lease on its first physical space, a small storefront two blocks from the truck's best lunch stop. Rent begins in ten weeks whether the dining room is finished or not, and the build-out — a kitchen line, a service counter and a printed menu board — costs more than the funding that is left.

PINEHILL MARKET, a regional grocery chain, has offered a large payment up front for a frozen retail version of the truck's signature dumplings, sold in its forty stores under the grocer's own store brand. That payment covers the build-out with room to spare. Filling the order takes the crew's two cooks every Friday and Saturday, which are the nights the truck parks at the RIVER LOT night market.

That market spot is where the company started. Its organizer holds the spot for the truck and keeps a waiting list of vendors who want it, and the crowd there posts the videos that carry the brand's name across social media. Taking the grocery order gives up the spot and puts the dumplings in freezer cases with no mention of GOLDEN HOUR DUMPLINGS on the package.

Opening the storefront on the cash the company has left instead means a bare dining room, a shorter menu and rent running for weeks before the doors open. The investor (judge) wants your recommendation on how to fund the storefront and how the brand would be positioned either way. The investor (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:

You put in the company's first and only round of funding two years ago, and you meet the general manager each month. You want to hear whether the company should take the PINEHILL MARKET order or open the storefront on the cash it has left, and you want to hear exactly how that recommendation would be carried out.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
